neighbours.label: the closing piece of a capitalised fixed scientific name (Periodic Table, Carbon Monoxide, Hydrogen Peroxide)
fire: In chemistry class we coloured in a blank Periodic Table for homework.
Firefighters warned residents about the dangers of Carbon Monoxide poisoning.
The nurse cleaned the cut with a little Hydrogen Peroxide.
Every lab wall seems to have a poster of the Periodic Table on it.
Our textbook explains how Sodium Chloride forms a crystal lattice.
The detector beeps loudly when Carbon Monoxide levels rise.
Mendeleev arranged the elements into the first Periodic Table in 1869.
Bottles of Hydrogen Peroxide should be stored away from sunlight.
quiet: In chemistry class we coloured in a blank world map for homework.
Firefighters warned residents about the dangers of candles left burning.
The nurse cleaned the cut with a little warm water.
Every lab wall seems to have a safety poster on it.
Our textbook explains how ice forms a crystal lattice.
The detector beeps loudly when smoke levels rise.
Mendeleev arranged his notes into a thick notebook in 1869.
Bottles of cooking oil should be stored away from sunlight.
